annual_frequency.note: HURDAT2 analysis centered on downtown Norfolk (36.85N, 76.29W), 1975-2024: 12 tropical cyclones at tropical-storm strength (>=34 kt) passed within 50 nm = 0.24/yr; within 100 nm: 38 at TS strength (0.76/yr) and 9 at hurricane strength (0.18/yr). Longer 1851-2024 record gives 0.26/yr (TS within 50 nm) and 0.21/yr (hurricane within 100 nm). FEMA NRI hurricane annualized frequency for Norfolk = 0.237 (VB 0.243, Chesapeake 0.242). Implication: ~4.8 tropical-storm-or-stronger passages within 50 nm, and ~3.6 hurricanes within 100 nm, over a 20-year roof life. Max wind is the storm's peak intensity inside the radius, not the wind measured at the site.

perils.severity_note: Direct hits are rare: since 1975 only Charley 1986 (70 kt) and Irene 2011 (65 kt) were at hurricane strength within 50 nm; Isabel 2003 (65 kt, closest 68 nm) and Floyd 1999 were within 100 nm. Hurricane dominates NRI building loss for every jurisdiction (Norfolk building EAL $13.0M/yr). ASCE 7-22 Risk Cat II basic wind speed for Norfolk ZIPs is reported at roughly 120-125 mph (eastern VA 115-130 mph) - per search summary of windloadcalc.com, not verified against the ASCE Hazard Tool.

code_triggers.text: Virginia enforces the Uniform Statewide Building Code (USBC), whose Part I Virginia Construction Code and Part II Virginia Existing Building Code (VEBC) are based on the ICC I-codes (current cycle believed to be the 2021 editions; Virginia amendments NOT verified this session). Model 2021 IEBC provisions (read directly): Sec. 705 (General) - reroofing materials/methods must comply with IBC Ch. 15, but existing low-slope roofs need not meet the 1/4:12 (2%) minimum slope, and need not add secondary (overflow) drains/scuppers if positive drainage exists; existing secondary drains may not be removed. Sec. 705 (Roof replacement) - roof replacement means removal of ALL existing layers down to the deck. Sec. 705 (Roof recover) - recover (overlay) is permitted per manufacturer instructions; coatings over BUR, mod bit, single-ply, SPF and metal are allowed without tear-off. Sec. 705 (Roof recover exceptions) - recover is PROHIBITED where the existing roof is water-soaked or deteriorated so it is not an adequate base, where the covering is slate/clay/cement/asbestos-cement tile, or where the roof already has two or more applications of any roof covering. Sec. 705 (Reinstallation of materials) - rusted/damaged flashing, edge metal and drain outlets may not be reinstalled; BUR aggregate may not be reused. Sec. 706 (Structural) - if an alteration raises gravity load >5%, structure must be upgraded, except a second roof layer of <=3 psf over a single existing layer. Sec. 706 (Roof diaphragms resisting wind loads in high-wind regions) - where >50% of roofing is removed and Vult >130 mph, roof diaphragm and roof-to-wall connections must be evaluated (Norfolk-area Vult is reported at ~120-125 mph, so this likely does not trigger - verify by site). Energy: IEBC Sec. 708 (Energy conservation, minimum requirements) requires Level 1 alterations (which include reroofing) to meet IECC requirements 'as they relate to new construction only', i.e., a roof replacement generally must bring above-deck insulation up to current IECC/Virginia energy-code roof R-values; the specific R-value and any Virginia amendments/exceptions were NOT verified this session. Note: the damage-percentage 'replace whole roof' rule (e.g., Florida's 25% rule) is not a model-IEBC provision; no Virginia equivalent was found.
